text:
Alex: Heads-up — billing alarm went off at 02:03 UTC, GPU spend +230% day-over-day. BillingBot reported a large cluster of new instances under 'on-demand' line items. Link: https://console.cloud.google.com/billing/exports (redacted)
BillingBot: exported line items for the period: \n- Compute Engine: N1_STANDARD_16 — $42k\n- Compute Engine: GPU-attached (rtx-series) — $8k\n- Commitment discounts applied: 0% for the N1 line items (possible scope mismatch)
Maria: I think I see the root cause — the cluster-autoscaler kept scaling a CPU-only nodepool instead of our GPU pool. The CPU pool hit quota and kept spinning more nodes, hence the on-demand spike.
Tariq: Did something change in node labels or autoscaler selectors in last night's infra PR? I remember a refactor of the node pool module.
Jonah: I pushed a change that replaced label `gpu=true` with `accelerator=rtx6000` in the terraform node pool module. Snippet from the PR:
```
resource "google_container_node_pool" "inference" {
  node_config {
    labels = {
      accelerator = "rtx6000"
    }
  }
}
```
Jonah: autoscaler config still expects `gpu:true` as the selector, so it didn't detect the GPU pool and fell back to the CPU pool.
Maria: yep — autoscaler pod logs show "no matching nodegroup found for nodeSelector gpu=true" and continued scaling the other pool. That explains idle committed GPUs + extra CPU spend.
Alex: Oof. That also explains why our committed/reserved GPU reservations were unused — and why the commitment discount didn't apply to the bulk of the new instances.
Tariq: Also saw some of the new nodes launched in us-east1 due to fallback/overflow when us-central1 quotas were hit. Some of our commitments are regional to us-central1 only, so those discounts didn't apply in us-east1.
Maria: Commands I ran: `kubectl -n kube-system logs deployment/cluster-autoscaler | grep "no matching"` and `kubectl get nodes -L gpu,accelerator -o wide` — shows many nodes with no gpu label.
Jonah: Immediate actions I'm doing now: 1) revert the label rename in the node pool terraform module (PR up), 2) patch autoscaler to accept both selectors (`gpu=true` OR `accelerator=*`) temporarily.
Jonah: Patch I plan to apply to the autoscaler deployment:
```
- --node-group-auto-discovery=kubernetes.io/cluster=redwood,labels=gpu=true
+ --node-group-auto-discovery=kubernetes.io/cluster=redwood,labels=gpu=true;labels=accelerator
```
Maria: Finance note — we need to reconcile line items with reservations and decide whether to convert some commitments to region-flex or change scope. Also add tags so future billing export can map to product teams.
Alex: Can we estimate the hit? BillingBot: preliminary export shows ~18 hours of excess CPU instances (~120 instances average) charged as on-demand. Rough estimate $14k over 18h.
Tariq: I'll also audit autoscaler fallback policies and quota alerts — we should fail fast instead of cross-region spillover. Add a guard to stop cross-region scaling unless explicitly allowed.
Maria: File created: INFRA-1921 (root cause: node label mismatch -> autoscaler scaled wrong pool). Assign Jonah to rollback and Maria to billing reconciliation. Alex to coordinate with Finance.
Alex: Quick timeline: rollback now, confirm GPU nodes come up and autoscaler shifts within 20m, then run billing export for reconciliation. @Jonah @Maria please update thread with timestamps when done. :eyes:
Jonah: Reverting terraform and kicking apply now. Will update when nodes show `accelerator=rtx6000` label.
Maria: I'll start the billing export and tag affected line items with `incident:INFRA-1921` and send to Finance.
BillingBot: FYI — scheduled report queued, will post CSV to shared drive when ready. :white_check_mark:
Tariq: Follow-ups: (1) make autoscaler selector resilient to label renames, (2) add a unit test in infra CI to catch label drift, (3) review reservation scope and consider converting some commitments to multi-region or zonal where appropriate.
Alex: Thanks everyone. Please add the exact commit/PR links in INFRA-1921 and mark as P0 for the billing impact. :thumbsup:
